dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between a shallow dip and a deep dip (odd vs even 6 times deeper) and the individual transits have very different depths, including one very shallow event plus a sector-to-sector depth jump from 1220 ppm to 2200 ppm between TESS-SPOC and QLP. That is what a nearby eclipsing binary blended in at twice the period looks like, not a planet. No on-target centroid or RV data rule out a background blend, but the depth pattern alone makes the planet an unlikely explanation.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly (depth_odd_ppm 362.7 vs depth_even_ppm 2238, depth_ratio 6.2, depth_difference_ppm 1875), with sector_oe_max_sigma 4.311 and sector_oe_same_sign_share 1. Points to a binary at twice the 12.6 d period (25.2 d).

4 transits individually inconsistent (chi2 25.654423849577576, dof 3). Near-gap has epoch -59 BTJD 1340.914 at 363 ppm sigma -4.3, but share_of_top_3 0.989 concentrates signal in few events; transit depths do not form a coherent planet depth.

p_constant_all 0.004214883778867774, depth changes 55.34% between sectors: TESS-SPOC depth_ppm 1247 err_ppm 225 vs QLP depth_ppm 2201 err_ppm 246. Product-dependent depths indicate systematic/bias from different apertures, not stable planet depth.
No significant secondary at half phase and secondary_over_bump 1.031, so no stellar eclipse confirmation. Combined with odd/even and depth scatter, planet cannot be favoured.
